maya: Hey team — hitting a reproducible TP all-reduce latency spike on the 8-shard nightly run. Timeline + microbench attached. Observed pattern: all-reduce tail latency jumps when per-rank message size is in the ~0.5MB–2MB window.
maya: Quick paste from the microbench (per-rank message bytes vs allreduce latency):
```
bytes   median_ms   p95_ms
64KB    0.6         1.1
256KB   1.8         3.0
512KB   6.4         12.7  <-- big jump
1MB     9.8         22.1
2MB     14.5        34.0
4MB     18.2        40.3
```
maya: Wall-time timeline shows long gaps where device compute is idle waiting on NCCL calls. Bandwidth counter looks saturated but latency per-chunk is higher than expected. I also see frequent small sub-chunks in traces (we chunk at 128KB currently).
maya: Command used: `python infra/bench/allreduce_micro.py --tp 8 --msg-chunk 131072 --iters 200 --profile timeline.json`
liam: Hmm — that mid-size cliff smells like chunk-alignment / fragmentation overhead. If our chunk size doesn't tile the message evenly across the ring/tree, we get extra rendezvous steps. Did you try increasing chunk size to 512KB or lowering it to avoid leftovers? Also try forcing a different NCCL algorithm to see behavior differences (ring vs tree).
maya: I tried 256KB and 512KB chunks locally — 512KB reduced p95 by ~20% for the 1MB case, but 4MB got slightly worse. Forcing algorithm to tree improved 512KB p95 by another ~10% on this topology.
sasha: Two other suspects: (1) KV cache replication pattern — we sometimes replicate large key blobs across TP ranks at attention build time which can turn lots of small buffers into medium-sized all-reduces; (2) kernel-selection mispredict: a few layers are using a slower matmul path for seq=2048 and that shifts when all-reduce runs relative to compute.
kevin: For overlap: are we waiting for full layer grads before starting all-reduce? If so, switch to async-grad-reduce (start reduce on chunk-ready) and make sure CUDA streams are configured for overlap. Also check that we don't serialize reductions on the main stream (I saw a few `cudaStreamSynchronize` in the perf trace right before NCCL calls).
maya: Good catch — the runtime currently does a flush-sync at layer boundaries in the fallback path. I'll toggle async-reduce and re-run.
liam: Also try this env/launch pattern for an A/B:
```
export TP=8
export NCCL_ALGO=tree
export ALLREDUCE_CHUNK_BYTES=524288
python serve/runtime_perf_test.py --tp $TP --iters 300
```
liam: If tree + 512KB chunk gives consistent win on the 1MB-2MB range, we probably want a heuristic: for per-rank message in [256KB, 2MB] prefer tree with chunk=512KB, otherwise default to ring + larger chunk.
sasha: Agree. We should also add a KV-cache probe: when sending KV updates, measure number of contiguous bytes and pick a chunking strategy that aligns to L1/L2 page sizes for the NIC to avoid leftover fragments.
kevin: I've put a quick perf checklist in the infra channel: make sure NCCL topo is correct (no unexpected NVLink/PCIe hops), set `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` for the reproducer, and confirm GPU clocks aren't down-clocking during the run (we saw that yesterday on the lab machines).
infra-bot: Note: scheduled maintenance on p-cluster-3 tomorrow 03:00 UTC — runs on that cluster will be noisy. (automated)
maya: Re-run results after async-reduce + chunk=512KB + NCCL_ALGO=tree: p95 for 1MB dropped from 22.1ms -> 12.4ms. 4MB case regressed by ~6%. So trade-off confirmed.
maya: Action items: 1) we add a quick heuristic to pick alg/chunk by per-rank msg size, 2) add KV-cache size probe to avoid generating mid-sized fragmented messages, 3) remove the fallback flush-sync path and add layered async-reduce, 4) run full nightly on p-cluster-4 (non-maintenance) and report.
liam: I'll draft the heuristic PR and include microbench harness tests. Thanks for the repro and numbers — nice triage.
sasha: I'll open a follow-up to add the KV probe + instrument the streaming allocator so we can see fragmentation histograms.
kevin: I'll coordinate the cluster run and check NVLink topo. If everyone OK, I'll kick off the full nightly once PRs land.
maya: Thanks all — attaching timeline.json link and the microbench output here: https://internal.prod/reports/1794025678/timeline.json (perf-attach).
